label: Elementary Differential Geometry
notes: Open the chapter. Information geometry studies families of probability distributions as differentiable manifolds, so we begin with the differential-geometric language the book will use. The deck follows printed pages 1 through 24 and introduces manifolds, charts, tangent vectors, Riemannian metrics, and affine connections in the concrete setting needed for statistics.

label: Manifolds and Charts
notes: Define a smooth manifold as a set covered by coordinate charts whose overlaps are smooth. Emphasize that a statistical model, a parametrized family of distributions, is exactly such a manifold with the parameter serving as a coordinate system. Coordinate changes correspond to reparametrizations of the model, which must leave geometric quantities invariant.

label: Tangent Vectors
notes: Introduce tangent vectors as directional derivatives and the tangent space at a point as their span. A basis is given by the coordinate partial derivatives. In the statistical setting tangent vectors are identified with score functions, the derivatives of the log-likelihood, which links geometry directly to estimation theory.

label: Riemannian Metric
notes: Define a Riemannian metric as a smoothly varying inner product on tangent spaces, giving lengths and angles. In information geometry the canonical metric is the Fisher information matrix, which measures how distinguishable nearby distributions are. This metric makes the manifold of distributions into a genuine geometric space.

label: Affine Connections
notes: Introduce affine connections and covariant differentiation, which let us compare tangent vectors at different points and define geodesics and parallel transport. The Christoffel symbols encode the connection in coordinates. Information geometry will exploit a whole family of connections, not just the Levi-Civita one, in the next chapters.

label: Recap
notes: Close the chapter. Manifolds and charts model parametrized families, tangent vectors become score functions, the Fisher metric measures distinguishability, and affine connections provide differentiation along the manifold. These elementary tools set the stage for the geometric structure of statistical models developed in Chapter 02.
